steps.message:
Lena Kovalchuk in the System Operations Center plans to issue Permission to Operate for Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) on 08/04/2025, the date Corwyn Realty Partners asked for. She has asked the DER Program Office whether anything on the record stands in the way, and she will issue or hold on the strength of the Office's answer.

Draft a memo to Lena as a Word document, working from the record as it stands at 07/14/2025, for the Office's reviewing engineer (P.E.) to sign. Tell her whether Permission to Operate can issue on 08/04/2025, one way or the other, and give the basis. For anything on the record that stands in the way, say what it is, what it rests on, what has to be done about it and by whom, and whether that can be done before that date. Save it as /filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx.

Four matters are under separate review and are not for this memo: the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering); the POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records); the site's queue position (Meera Vellanki, under the weekly queue reports); and the system impact study and its conditions (Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records). Nothing else is under separate review.

Then open one work package for the site in OpenProject's DER Program Backlog Review project recording your determination and anything that has to be settled before Permission to Operate and by whom, including anything Corwyn Realty Partners has to settle.

INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex · Rev Final · Date 09/12/2024 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
Agreement No.: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex
Project: Corwyn Office Complex PV
Application No.: PXA-2023-0629
This Interconnection Service Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (the "Company"), and Corwyn Realty Partners, with offices at 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR (the "Interconnection Customer"), each a "Party" and together the "Parties." This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
RECITALS
WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2023-0629, on 07/11/2023, for a 700 kW (ac) photovoltaic generating facility on five parking canopies at the Corwyn Office Complex, to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system on Feeder ALN-072;
WHEREAS, the Company completed its review of the application under the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and approved the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in this Agreement;
WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms part of the terms of interconnection service under this Agreement;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Company's filed tariff (the "Tariff") and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the "DIS").
1.2 "Facility" means the generating facility described in Exhibit B: the five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, one on each of the five parking canopies, together with the Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B.
1.3 "Point of Interconnection" or "POI" means the point on Feeder ALN-072 at which the Facility connects to the Company's distribution system, at the Company's POI recloser in the north lot. The point of common coupling coincides with the Point of Interconnection.
1.4 "Company's Facilities" means the POI recloser, the remote terminal unit (RTU) and revenue meter RM-0629 described in Article 5.
1.5 "Permission to Operate" means the Company's written permission for parallel operation of the Facility under Article 6.
1.6 "Standards" means the Company standards identified in Section 4.1.
ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
2.1 Project designation. Corwyn Office Complex PV (Application PXA-2023-0629).
2.2 Interconnection Customer. Corwyn Realty Partners.
2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation on five parking canopies over the surface lots beside the parking structure.
2.4 Capacity. 700 kW (ac), export at the Point of Interconnection.
2.5 Feeder. ALN-072, 13.2 kV.
2.6 Material terms. The capacity and the Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement (Tariff §12.6; DIS §7).
ARTICLE 3 — TERM
3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 09/12/2024, the date on which the last of the Parties executed it.
3.2 Term. This Agreement remains in force from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality and dispute resolution survive any termination of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 4 — STANDARDS
4.1 The Facility shall be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated and maintained in conformity with DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time.
4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency, the following order governs: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the Standards; (iii) the body of this Agreement and its Exhibits.
ARTICLE 5 — INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
5.1 Company's Facilities. The Company provides, owns and operates the POI recloser (DPS-07 §4.2), the RTU (TCS-02 §3) and revenue meter RM-0629 with 13.2 kV primary metering at the Point of Interconnection, at the Interconnection Customer's cost under the construction work order.
5.2 Interconnection Customer's facilities. The Interconnection Customer provides, owns and maintains the interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B and the site provisions for the Company's Facilities (equipment pad, primary conductors to the recloser terminals, and the station service and communications entrance for the RTU) as specified in the Company's construction package.
5.3 Access. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company access at all times to the Point of Interconnection, the revenue meter and the Facility's disconnects.
ARTICLE 6 — COMMISSIONING AND PERMISSION TO OPERATE
6.1 Witness test. Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility under the Company's Witness Test & Waiver Procedure, under a Distribution Operations switching order and with the System Operations Center observing. At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.
6.2 Permission to operate. Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, telemetry is live at the System Operations Center, the witness test is complete, and the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities.
6.3 First parallel operation. The first parallel operation after permission to operate is observed by the System Operations Center with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision (DPS-07 §6.3).
ARTICLE 7 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
7.1 Metering. Revenue-quality bidirectional metering is provided at the Point of Interconnection, owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and sealed at all times.
7.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer provides, at its cost, the provisions for the Company's RTU and makes available the analog and status points that TCS-02 requires. Live telemetry at the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate, and any loss of telemetry after permission to operate is reported and remedied as TCS-02 provides.
ARTICLE 8 — OPERATION
8.1 Operating representatives. The Company's operating representative is the System Operations Center. The Interconnection Customer's operating representative is the Corwyn Office Complex property management office, reachable at all times at (612) 555-0827. Each Party gives the other its operating notices through these representatives.
8.2 Loss of the utility source. On any loss of the utility source at the Point of Interconnection, the Facility shall cease to energize within 2.0 seconds.
8.3 Disconnection by the Company. The Company may open the POI recloser and keep the Facility disconnected for a system emergency, for work on its distribution system, on loss of telemetry, or where the Facility fails to meet this Agreement, with notice to the Interconnection Customer where practicable.
8.4 Reconnection. After the Company has opened the POI recloser, the Facility is placed back in parallel only on the release of the System Operations Center.
8.5 Clearances. On the Company's request the Interconnection Customer opens and padlocks the Facility's disconnects identified in Exhibit B for a clearance and keeps them open until the Company releases the clearance.
8.6 Planned outages. The Interconnection Customer gives the System Operations Center five (5) business days' notice of any planned outage of the Facility longer than one day.
8.7 Changes. The Interconnection Customer makes no change to the Facility's equipment or settings without the Company's written consent under Article 12.
ARTICLE 9 — MAINTENANCE AND RECORDS
9.1 The Interconnection Customer maintains the Facility in accordance with the Standards and the manufacturers' instructions.
9.2 The Interconnection Customer tests the Facility's protective functions on a schedule not longer than that of comparable Company equipment and makes the records available to the Company on request (DPS-07 §6.4).
9.3 The Interconnection Customer keeps operating and maintenance records for the Facility for the term of this Agreement and makes them available to the Company on request.
ARTICLE 10 — PAYMENT
10.1 The Interconnection Customer pays for the Company's Facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement and Tariff §12.5.
10.2 Invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
ARTICLE 11 — LIABILITY AND INSURANCE
11.1 Each Party is responsible for the facilities it owns under this Agreement.
11.2 The Interconnection Customer indemnifies the Company against third-party claims arising from the operation of the Facility, except to the extent caused by the Company's negligence.
11.3 During the term the Interconnection Customer maintains commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and provides a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request.
ARTICLE 12 — AMENDMENTS
12.1 No term of this Agreement may be modified or waived except by an instrument in writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.
12.2 Changes to the capacity or the Point of Interconnection are governed by DIS §7. Other changes to the Facility are made by change order under Section 12.1.
ARTICLE 13 — NOTICES
13.1 Notices under this Agreement are in writing and are delivered by hand, by certified mail, or by e-mail with confirmation of receipt.
13.2 To the Company: DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities, 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA; der.program@alleniom.com; (612) 555-0100.
13.3 To the Interconnection Customer: Corwyn Realty Partners, attention Director of Property Operations, 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR; (612) 555-0827.
13.4 Operating notices under Article 8 pass between the operating representatives named in Section 8.1.
ARTICLE 14 — SIGNATURES
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the dates set forth below, this Agreement being effective as of the date last executed.

EXHIBIT A — POINT OF INTERCONNECTION
Feeder ALN-072, 13.2 kV, three-phase. The Company's POI recloser and revenue meter RM-0629 are on the Company's pole at the north lot. The Interconnection Customer's 13.2 kV primary conductors run from the Point of Interconnection to primary switch PSW-1 and step-up transformer T-1 in the equipment yard.
EXHIBIT B — FACILITY AND INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
B.1 Generating equipment. Five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, INV-C1 to INV-C5, 140 kW (ac) each at 480 V, three-phase, one on each of canopies C1 to C5; 700 kW (ac) in all. The inverters provide the interconnection protective functions by their certified functions (DIS Table 5-1, Category 2) and operate at the IEEE 1547-2018 Category III default settings and constant power factor 1.00 unless the Company directs otherwise in writing.
B.2 Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities. Inverter ac disconnects AD-C1 to AD-C5, one beside each inverter; PV switchboard SWBD-PV with five 225 A inverter breakers and a 1,200 A main breaker; step-up transformer T-1, 750 kVA, 13.2 kV grounded wye to 480Y/277 V; primary switch PSW-1 with current-limiting fuses; the 13.2 kV primary conductors from PSW-1 to the Point of Interconnection.
B.3 Monitoring. The PV monitoring cabinet DAS-1 is the Interconnection Customer's own monitoring and is not part of the Company's telemetry.

INTERNAL MEMORANDUM

FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
/s/
Harriet Ngoyi

§12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:
(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
MW);
(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).
The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.
Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
Program scope.

§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.
§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
active queue without further action of the Company.
For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
as non-business days and shall not be counted:

notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
the date of that written notice.
For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
consequences, and different cure paths.
Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

§12.6 Interconnection Service Agreement
Interconnection service shall commence only upon execution of an Interconnection Service
Agreement (“ISA”) and the Company's written Permission to Operate. Material terms of an
executed ISA, including but not limited to nameplate facility capacity and the designated point of
interconnection, may not be modified by amendment. Post-execution changes to such material
terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
Interconnection Standard.
§12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.

identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1.
The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2.
Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3.
Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4.
Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.

5.
The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:
•
the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
•
for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;

Page 3
•
for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;
•
the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;
•
correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.

current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards

DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:

• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);

are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.

IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.
§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

--- PAGE 4 ---

The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
certification and Control Narrative are always required.

§6 Monitoring and Control
Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common

aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.
§4   COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1   Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•
a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
•
b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
•
c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.
Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2   SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3   Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.

DIS-01 §3.4.

Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 5
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.

--- PAGE 6 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 6
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
§7.6   Physical security
The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.
End of TCS-02.

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. Our high school's building-systems curriculum was also structured around students being able to observe the array in operation from the beginning of the term; that piece of the school year is now at risk of slipping into the second semester or being cut altogether.

You will by now have received the Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, signed by Executive Director Alden Pryce, escalating this same set of concerns on behalf of the District and thirteen other League members. Brookfen USD is one of the members named in that letter and stands fully behind the requests it contains. This message is not a substitute for the League's letter; it is intended to make the District's individual position, and the specifics of our two sites, unmistakable to your office.

What I am asking for, directly, is this: in the next allocation of the equipment your program office is holding up as the constraint — the RTU / telemetry units your staff have referenced in prior calls — I am asking Alleniom Utilities to advance the District's two waiting arrays ahead of the other sites presently competing for those units. Brookfen North completed construction on 04/18/2025 and Brookfen West on 05/23/2025. Both are public school facilities. Both have children returning to the building in eight weeks. Neither array can wait for a second or third delivery cycle without meaningful harm to the District's fiscal position and to the educational program these systems were installed to support.

If there is a formal process for requesting that our two sites be advanced in your next equipment allocation, please tell me what that process is and I will follow it today. If there is not, please treat this message as our written request under whatever mechanism your program uses to weigh these decisions, and please confirm receipt.

I am copying Ms. Whitcomb and Ms. Ngoyi so that this request is on the record with senior distribution operations and regulatory affairs, and so that no one at your program office is later in a position to say the District did not put this in writing in time.

I would like a written reply — not a call-back, a written reply — by close of business Friday, 07/11/2025. Silence past that date will require the District to raise this matter again through the League and, if necessary, directly with the Commission's Energy Resources Division, whose staff we understand is already tracking this program.

I am available at (612) 448-0311 during District business hours if it would help to talk any of this through. I would strongly prefer to resolve it with your office.

Regards,

Rosa Camarena
Facilities Director
Brookfen Unified School District
1725 Grantway Drive, Brookfen, Alleron 12BR

Dear Ms. Whitcomb:
On behalf of the Alleron Municipal League and the fourteen member communities identified below, I write to
convey our formal and collective concern regarding the continued and, in our view, unreasonable delays
affecting commercial-scale solar interconnection projects currently stalled within Alleniom Utilities’ Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection program. This letter follows repeated informal outreach by individual
member staff to your DER Program Office over the preceding several months, outreach which has not produced
the clarity or the timely progress our members need in order to close out their local capital projects.
The League is writing on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts across the state of Alleron whose
commercial-scale solar projects — commissioned in good faith with voter-approved bond proceeds, adopted
capital budgets, energy-savings performance contracts, and in several instances state and federal grant awards
Additional League members with projects in the same posture have asked to be represented collectively through
this correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been
reviewed and approved by the applicable local governing body, financed through public procurement, and
constructed by licensed contractors under permits issued by the relevant authority having jurisdiction.
The projects at issue are not speculative or exploratory. They range in size from approximately 500 kW to nearly
1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,
public libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical
and electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing
energized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s
authorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay
defers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school
boards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.
Our members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the
Company’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment
procurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical
requirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an

League’s executive office, and designated representatives of the affected members, to be scheduled at the

For your awareness, a copy of this letter has been provided to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC),
Energy Resources Division, for the Division’s information. The League has taken this step not as a matter of
confrontation but out of a good-faith obligation to keep the Commission’s staff apprised of a program-level
concern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the
Company’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom

confident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards
regard it.

Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.
§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)	applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)	queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)	staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)	the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)	the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)	the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)	a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)	be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)	be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)	identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)	state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.	Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.	Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.	Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.	On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.	Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)	The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)	The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)	The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)	Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)	the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)	at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)	the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)	be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)	be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)	identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)	state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)	state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)	state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)	“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)	Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)	The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
(d)	Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)	mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)	record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)	preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)	the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)	for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)	for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
(d)	the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
(e)	any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
§4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
(a)	application identifier and site;
(b)	closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
(c)	closure date;
(d)	case handler; and
(e)	reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.
§4.3  Withdrawal-Notice Log
The DER Program Office shall maintain a running Withdrawal-Notice Log recording every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation issued. The log shall include, at minimum: application identifier; site; date of issuance; method of service; response deadline (computed under §3.4); response received (date and disposition, if any); and closure date (if any). The log is subject to periodic reconciliation against the on-hold queue report; unreconciled entries shall be brought to the attention of the Manager, Interconnection Studies.
§4.4  Retention
Case files and log entries shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records retention schedule for regulated interconnection records. Records shall not be purged, redacted, or altered while an application remains open, while a response window under §3 is running, or while the closure is within the period during which reconsideration may be sought.
§4.5  Audit and Reporting
The Manager, Interconnection Studies shall be prepared, on request of Regulatory Affairs, to produce for any closed application: the closure basis; the writing(s) supporting the closure basis; the queue-date determination for any successor application; and, where applicable, the notice, proof of service, and 30 business-day computation. Reports to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission concerning queue closures shall be prepared from the withdrawal-notice log and the queue-management system entries described above.

1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.
