4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.

5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the

affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.

§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.

Classification: Technical Standard — Distributed Energy Resource Interconnection
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Planning; Standards Engineering;
Regulatory Affairs
§1   Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.
§2   Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a)  all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b)  all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a)  sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b)  capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c)  domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.
§3   Screens

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
MEMORANDUM
1.  Question presented
Corwyn Realty Partners requested written permission to operate Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629 — 700 kW ac, five parking-canopy inverters on feeder ALN-072) from 08/04/2025 (request of Nadia Ferreira-Holt, Director of Property Operations, 07/10/2025). You asked the DER Program Office whether anything on the record stands in the way, and indicated you will issue or hold on the strength of the Office’s answer. This memorandum is that answer, from the record as it stands at 07/14/2025.
2.  Determination
Permission to Operate can issue on 08/04/2025.  On the in-scope record — the matters the DER Program Office reviewing engineer is responsible for — nothing stands in the way. Two things remain to be confirmed before the SOC authorizes first parallel operation, and both can be closed before 08/04/2025: (i) the four matters under separate review listed in §5, which are outside this memorandum and are owned by the named groups; and (ii) Corwyn’s certificate of insurance under ISA Article 11.3 (none on file), which Corwyn can furnish on the Company’s request. On the in-scope record alone there is no basis to hold.
3.  Governing standard
The Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, executed 09/12/2024) governs. ISA Article 6.2 conditions Permission to Operate on four things: (i) the Company’s facilities commissioned and accepted; (ii) telemetry live at the System Operations Center; (iii) the witness test complete; and (iv) final approval of the customer’s facilities by the authority having jurisdiction. Live telemetry is independently required by TCS-02 §5 (no PTO without live telemetry; the SOC Shift Supervisor confirms compliance at the time PTO is requested). A construction-payment default places the project on hold in the queue (Tariff §12.5).
4.  In-scope findings — nothing stands in the way
Working from the record as of 07/14/2025, the in-scope ISA Article 6.2 conditions are satisfied and no hold, default, or shortfall blocks the site:
Witness test complete and passed.  Witness test WT-0629-01 was held 07/08/2025 under Distribution Operations switching order DO-2025-0677 with the SOC observing. All test points on inverters INV-C1 to INV-C5 and on the Facility passed — voltage and frequency trip tests, ride-through verified value-by-value against the IEEE 1547-2018 Category III table, anti-islanding (output to zero in 0.39–0.46 s against the 2.0 s limit), and enter-service (302–304 s against the 300 s minimum). The record is signed by the witness engineer (M. Halbrook, P.E.), the commissioning coordinator (S. Rennick), and the commissioning agent (K. Osei, Brantley Electric Company). A witness test rather than a waiver was required because the SWBD-PV breakers are protective devices not carried on CEL-2025-Q2 (Witness Test & Waiver Procedure ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3, §§3–4.1); the signed witness-test disposition satisfies the commissioning-record prerequisite under ENG-PRC-014 §4.3.
AHJ final approval of the customer’s facilities.  The City of Wrenford issued electrical permit WEP-25-0317 on 05/27/2025 and gave final approval on 07/02/2025 (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector), stating the permitted work “may be energized and operated in parallel with the utility on the utility’s permission.”
Revenue meter.  RM-0629 (13.2 kV primary metering at the point of interconnection) was set and tested by Alleniom Metering and delivered with received registers verified on 07/08/2025.
Certified equipment.  The Vexlar VX-140C inverter is listed on the current Certified Equipment List, CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025), Inverters tab, row 18 (UL 1741-SB, effective 09/16/2024). Vexlar’s certificate of conformance VX-CC-25-0522 (05/22/2025) is on file — UL 1741-SB, IEEE 1547-2018 Category III — and the five unit serial numbers match the witness test record.
Customer telemetry provisions.  Drawing E-401 Rev C (06/24/2025) shows the inverter-to-RTU communications link (COM-RTU, per-inverter ac power and status for SCADA) and station AC service to the RTU enclosure through a 1.5 kVA online UPS rated for 5.5 h at the RTU load, exceeding the TCS-02 §3.4 minimum of four hours.
Live telemetry at the SOC.  The commissioning checklist (CX-CW-01 Rev 2, 07/14/2025) records that telemetry was live at the SOC, confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor (L. Kovalchuk) on 07/08/2025. Whether the underlying RTU installation and commissioning are accepted is a matter under separate review (§5) and is not opined on here.
No holds.  The site is not on the SOC PTO-Hold Log (DER-EQP-SOC-PTOH, 07/14/2025), not on the Standards Conflict Hold List (SCR-HL-004, 07/14/2025), and not on the Abnormality Hold List (07/14/2025).
No construction-payment default.  PXA-2023-0629 does not appear in the Construction Work-Order Payment Ledger (07/14/2025); there is no open invoice or open balance, and therefore no Tariff §12.5 construction-payment default.
Not awaiting utility equipment.  The site is not on the Completed Sites Awaiting Utility Equipment register (DER-EQP-COMPL Rev 3, 07/14/2025); the RTU and POI recloser are deployed at the site.
Active and not at risk of withdrawal.  The Active Queue Report (07/14/2025) carries PXA-2023-0629 in “commissioning” status (queue date 07/11/2023); the site is not on the on-hold report and has no Notice of Impending Withdrawal on the Withdrawal Notice Log (07/14/2025).
No aggregation issue.  The Existing-DER Register (07/14/2025) shows no DER at 2400 Corwyn Parkway; the 700 kW facility is commercial small-scale (DIS-01 Rev 4 §3, Table 3-1), consistent with the ISA.
5.  Matters under separate review (outside this memorandum)
Four matters are under separate review and are not addressed in this memorandum. I express no view on their substance and defer to their owners. Two of them underlie ISA Article 6.2 conditions (the Company’s facilities commissioned and accepted; telemetry live at the SOC), so the final go on those conditions rests with the named groups together with your own TCS-02 §5 confirmation:
Installation, configuration, and commissioning tests of the Company’s RTU and POI recloser — SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and Distribution Protection Engineering (N. Achterberg, P.E.).
POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study behind them — Distribution Protection Engineering (N. Achterberg, P.E.), which issued the settings and holds the study outside these records.
The site’s queue position — Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki), under the weekly queue reports.
The system impact study and its conditions — the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham), which holds them outside these records.
Nothing else is under separate review.
6.  Item to be settled before PTO — Corwyn Realty Partners
Certificate of insurance.  ISA Article 11.3 requires Corwyn to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence during the term (which began 09/12/2024) and to furnish a certificate on the Company’s request. No certificate is on file as of 07/14/2025. This is not an ISA Article 6.2 technical condition, and the ISA does not make it a freestanding PTO precondition; it is, however, a contractual prerequisite the Company should confirm before authorizing operation. What has to be done: the DER Program Office—Contracts requests the certificate and verifies coverage, and Corwyn Realty Partners furnishes a current $2,000,000 CGL certificate. It can be done before 08/04/2025; the DER Program Office—Contracts should request it now.
7.  Whether the open items can be closed before 08/04/2025
The date sought (08/04/2025) is about three weeks after the record date (07/14/2025). The four matters under separate review are reviews of work the in-scope commissioning record reflects was completed on or before 07/08/2025 (RTU end-to-end test and valid SCADA points; POI recloser site acceptance items 1–7; recloser settings issued 06/18/2025; telemetry live at the SOC), and the study is not carried on the SIS backlog (DPG-SIS-BL-2025-07), which is consistent with completion. There is therefore schedule room for each review to close before 08/04/2025; I express no view on the outcome of any of them. The certificate of insurance can be furnished within days on request. Each open item can accordingly be closed before 08/04/2025.
8.  Recommendation
Close the four matters under separate review through their owners and obtain Corwyn’s certificate of insurance under ISA Article 11.3. On the in-scope record, Permission to Operate can issue on 08/04/2025; nothing the DER Program Office reviewing engineer is responsible for stands in the way.
Respectfully,
/s/ M. Halbrook, P.E.
Reviewing Engineer, DER Program Office

On the in-scope record as of 07/14/2025, **Permission to Operate can issue on 08/04/2025 — nothing the DER Program Office reviewing engineer is responsible for stands in the way.** The in-scope ISA Article 6.2 conditions are satisfied: witness test complete and passed (WT-0629-01, 07/08/2025); City of Wrenford final approval of the customer's facilities (WEP-25-0317, 07/02/2025); revenue meter RM-0629 set, tested, and delivered. The site is on no hold (SOC PTO-hold log, standards-conflict hold list, abnormality hold list), has no construction-payment default (absent from the WO payment ledger), is not awaiting utility equipment, and its inverter and certificate of conformance are on the current CEL (CEL-2025-Q2, row 18).

## Items to be settled before Permission to Operate — and by whom

### A. Matters under separate review (outside the PTO memo; final go on ISA §6.2 conditions rests with these owners)
1. **RTU and POI recloser — installation, configuration, and commissioning tests** — SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and Distribution Protection Engineering (N. Achterberg, P.E.). Underlies ISA §6.2 "Company's facilities commissioned and accepted."
2. **POI recloser settings and protection coordination study** — Distribution Protection Engineering (N. Achterberg, P.E.); settings issued 06/18/2025, study held outside these records.
3. **Site queue position** — Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki), under the weekly queue reports.
4. **System impact study and its conditions** — DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham); held outside these records.

### B. Corwyn Realty Partners (customer) item
5. **Certificate of insurance** — ISA Article 11.3 requires commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence during the term (from 09/12/2024), certificate furnished on the Company's request; **none on file as of 07/14/2025.** Owner: **Corwyn Realty Partners** (furnish a current certificate) and **DER Program Office—Contracts** (request and verify). Not an ISA §6.2 technical condition; confirm before authorizing operation.

## Can each be done before 08/04/2025? — Yes
The four matters under separate review are reviews of work the in-scope commissioning record shows was completed on or before 07/08/2025 (RTU end-to-end test and valid SCADA points; POI recloser site acceptance items 1–7; recloser settings issued 06/18/2025; telemetry live at the SOC); ~3 weeks remain to 08/04/2025. The certificate of insurance can be furnished within days on request.

## Notes
- Four matters are under separate review and are not for the PTO memo; this work package records their owners so the SOC and the backlog review can track them to closure. Nothing else is under separate review.
